## Presentation Title
**ORIGIN: Ethiopia, the First Cup**  
*An editorial journey through highlands, ritual, harvest, and heritage*

## Style Direction
- Cinematic premium documentary with luxury travel-magazine polish — slow, atmospheric, tactile
- Feels like National Geographic meets Monocle, Kinfolk, and an Apple cultural keynote
- Warm, human, reverent, sensory: misty highlands, red coffee cherries, roasted smoke, handwoven textiles
- Avoid generic coffee-shop clichés, stock café imagery, flat history slides, tourist-board aesthetics
- Every frame should feel like a carefully art-directed film still from the birthplace of coffee

## Core Artistic Direction
- Full-bleed cinematic photography: Ethiopian highlands, farmers’ hands, coffee cherries, jebena ceremony, market textures, golden-hour landscapes
- Premium editorial typography: elegant serif hero titles, restrained sans-serif body, small uppercase mono captions like museum labels
- Earth-rich palette: roasted brown, ochre gold, clay red, parchment cream, deep forest green, charcoal black
- Layer subtle textures: film grain, handmade paper, woven textile patterns, coffee-stain washes, smoky ceremony haze
- Layout mood: asymmetrical magazine spreads, generous negative space, oversized pull quotes, image-led storytelling
- Use refined cultural details: hand-drawn origin maps, botanical coffee illustrations, minimal linework, archival-style annotations
- Animation energy: slow Ken Burns zooms, soft dissolves, drifting steam, gentle light leaks, map lines drawing organically
- Overall finish: premium, cinematic, intimate, heritage-focused — less “presentation,” more visual documentary essay

## Color Palette

**Abyssinian Espresso** `#2A1710` — primary deep background, title overlays, luxury contrast.  
**Roasted Clay** `#6B3F2A` — warm editorial panels, section dividers, map accents.  
**Bunna Gold** `#C99A55` — premium highlight, key lines, ceremony glow, icon details.  
**Highland Cream** `#F6EFE4` — page background, text areas, soft negative space.  
**Yirgacheffe Green** `#4F6F45` — origin-region accents, agricultural notes, subtle chart color.  
**Coffee Cherry Red** `#A53A2B` — emphasis marks, cherry visuals, pull quotes, data highlights.  
**Mist Blue Grey** `#9DA9A7` — highland atmosphere, secondary text, map terrain shading.  
**Jebena Black** `#12100E` — premium typography, silhouettes, cinematic depth.  
**Sunrise Amber** `#E0B06A` — golden-hour gradients, transition glow, photographic warmth.  
**Parchment Taupe** `#B8A48E` — editorial borders, captions, archival textures, timeline details.  

## Typography

**Hero Display: Canela Deck** — 72–110pt, light/regular, cinematic titles and poetic cover statements.  
**Editorial Serif: GT Sectra** — 38–64pt, medium, section openers, feature headlines, dramatic quotes.  
**Body Copy: Söhne** — 16–24pt, regular, narrative paragraphs, cultural context, slide descriptions.  
**Caption / Metadata: Söhne Mono** — 10–14pt, regular/medium, region labels, tasting notes, photo credits, coordinates.  
**Accent Script: Recia / Editorial New Italic** — 28–52pt, italic, sensory phrases, ceremony moments, emotional callouts.  

| Hierarchy | Size |
|---|---:|
| Hero | 88–110pt |
| Section | 52–72pt |
| Body | 18–22pt |
| Caption | 10–14pt |

## Layout System
- **12-column editorial grid** with cinematic asymmetry: oversized hero imagery, narrow text columns, and magazine-style pull quotes.
- **Full-bleed photography rule:** use edge-to-edge visuals for origin landscapes, coffee ceremonies, farmers, and macro bean shots; preserve clean negative space for typography.
- **Premium margin system:** 96–120px outer margins, 48px internal gutters, generous breathing room around captions and body text.
- **Composition types:** documentary hero frames, luxury editorial spreads, split-screen process layouts, map-led storytelling, portrait grids, and macro-detail panels.
- **Typography placement:** large serif headlines anchored bottom-left or top-right; small mono captions placed like museum labels along image edges.
- **Visual rhythm:** alternate immersive cinematic slides with refined editorial information slides to create a slow documentary pacing.

## Animation Style
- **Transitions:** soft cinematic cross-dissolves, slow fade-through-black, subtle parallax wipes inspired by documentary scene changes.
- **Entrance effects:** text fades in with gentle upward drift; captions appear last with restrained editorial timing.
- **Speed/easing:** slow, premium motion; 700–1200ms transitions using ease-in-out or cubic-bezier smoothness.
- **Photography motion:** Ken Burns pushes across highland landscapes, slow lateral pans over drying beds, micro-zooms into coffee cherries and roasted beans.
- **Map/diagram motion:** Ethiopian regions draw in with hand-inked line animation; flavor notes bloom outward like tasting aromas.
- **Atmospheric motion:** drifting steam, soft dust particles, golden-hour light leaks, and subtle film-grain shimmer.

## Visual Requirements
- **Photography style:** cinematic documentary, golden-hour natural light, shallow depth of field, tactile close-ups of hands, cherries, beans, jebena, and highland farms.
- **Portrait direction:** dignified farmer portraits with environmental context; intimate, respectful, unsentimental, premium magazine quality.
- **Illustration type:** hand-drawn cartographic accents, botanical coffee-plant sketches, small editorial icons inspired by field notebooks.
- **Diagram aesthetic:** elegant origin maps, processing timelines, roast spectrum, and flavor-wheel visuals using refined labels and restrained color.
- **Texture/overlay notes:** subtle film grain, warm paper texture, soft vignettes, transparent dust overlays, muted earth-toned gradients.
- **Color atmosphere:** roasted brown, highland green, sun-dried cherry red, parchment cream, smoke black, and golden Ethiopian sunset highlights.

## Slide-by-Slide Structure

**Slide 1 — Birthplace in the Mist**
- Mood: Cinematic, sacred, dawn-lit introduction — Ethiopia as coffee’s mythic origin, quiet and majestic like the opening frame of a premium documentary.
- Layout: Full-bleed landscape hero image with generous negative space in the upper sky; title anchored low-left in editorial magazine style; small documentary caption and coordinates placed bottom-right.
- Visual: 4K aerial view of mist rolling over Ethiopian highland coffee forests, early golden sunlight cutting through eucalyptus silhouettes, tiny village rooftops barely visible.
- FX: Slow Ken Burns push inward through the fog; subtle film grain; title fades in like opening credits; faint animated mist drifting across foreground.
- Color: Highland fog gray, roasted brown, muted forest green, antique gold, warm ivory highlights.
- Type: Large elegant serif title, refined and cinematic; small all-caps monospaced metadata line: “ETHIOPIA / EAST AFRICA / ORIGIN ALTITUDE 1,500–2,200M”.

**Slide 2 — The Legend of Kaldi**
- Mood: Mythic, intimate, storybook-documentary — a blend of oral tradition, folklore, and ancient discovery.
- Layout: Split editorial composition: left side cinematic illustration/photo-composite of Kaldi and goats; right side parchment-toned text panel with pull quote and minimal timeline marker.
- Visual: A young Ethiopian goat herder in the highlands watching energetic goats near red coffee cherries; softly painted realism mixed with photographic texture; hand-drawn botanical coffee branch overlay.
- FX: Gentle parallax between foreground cherries, Kaldi, and distant hills; glowing red coffee cherries pulse subtly; handwritten annotation lines draw themselves in.
- Color: Sun-baked ochre, cherry red, clay brown, parchment cream, deep shadow green.
- Type: Serif headline with poetic weight; italic pull quote oversized: “A small red fruit changed the rhythm of the world.” Supporting text in clean editorial sans.

**Slide 3 — The Coffee Map of Ethiopia**
- Mood: Exploratory, premium travel atlas — elegant, geographic, immersive, like a luxury magazine feature on terroir.
- Layout: Center-stage illustrated map of Ethiopia on warm paper texture; coffee regions radiate outward as floating labeled cards; small flavor notes placed like tasting annotations.
- Visual: Hand-drawn cartographic map highlighting Sidamo, Yirgacheffe, Harrar, Limu, Jimma, Guji, and Lekempti; delicate contour lines, altitude marks, coffee leaf sketches, tiny route lines tracing trade paths.
- FX: Map linework draws on in ink; region labels appear one by one with soft glow; subtle animated coffee-bean particles move along route lines.
- Color: Warm ivory paper, espresso ink, muted terracotta, botanical green, golden altitude contour accents.
- Type: Editorial serif title top-left; region names in small caps; flavor notes in handwritten-style annotations: “floral,” “citrus,” “winey,” “berry,” “spiced cocoa.”

**Slide 4 — The Highlands Remember**
- Mood: Misty, ancient, cinematic; the sense that coffee is not simply grown here, but remembered by the land.
- Layout: Full-bleed panoramic highland landscape with a narrow editorial text column floating on the left; small coordinate-style caption at bottom right.
- Visual: Dawn over Ethiopian coffee forests, soft fog moving between hills, distant farmers walking along terraced paths; documentary stillness with premium magazine restraint.
- FX: Slow Ken Burns push into the mist; faint animated contour lines appear like a topographic memory; text fades in like breath on glass.
- Color: Highland green, fog white, muted gold, deep soil brown; low-contrast cinematic grade with warm highlights and cool shadows.
- Type: Large elegant serif title stacked vertically on the left; small uppercase mono caption reading region, altitude, and harvest season.

**Slide 5 — Hands of the Harvest**
- Mood: Intimate, tactile, human; reverence for labor, craft, and inherited knowledge.
- Layout: Editorial split composition: oversized close-up image on the right, quiet negative space on the left with three short poetic text fragments.
- Visual: Macro documentary photograph of weathered hands selecting ripe red coffee cherries; shallow depth of field, skin texture, woven basket fibers, sunlight catching cherry skins.
- FX: Subtle parallax between hands, cherries, and background; tiny dust particles drift through golden light; handwritten annotation lines gently draw around selected cherries.
- Color: Sun-dried cherry red, warm ochre, roasted brown, linen cream; cherries act as the visual accent against earthy neutrals.
- Type: Refined serif headline in warm cream; small italic pull quote beneath; micro-caption in monospaced type along the image edge.

**Slide 6 — The Ceremony of Smoke and Time**
- Mood: Sacred, communal, slow-burning; a living ritual unfolding through aroma, flame, conversation, and hospitality.
- Layout: Cinematic horizontal triptych: roasting pan, incense smoke, jebena pouring; central image slightly larger like a film frame.
- Visual: Ethiopian coffee ceremony scene with buna being roasted over coals, incense curling upward, small cups arranged on a woven mat, warm room lit by firelight.
- FX: Smoke animation moves gently across the frame; ember glow pulses subtly; slide transition dissolves like steam rising from a cup.
- Color: Charcoal black, ember orange, clay red, woven straw beige, soft smoke gray; rich shadows with glowing amber highlights.
- Type: Title placed low and centered in elegant serif; ceremonial steps labeled in small uppercase editorial captions: roast, grind, brew, pour, share.

**Slide 7 — From Cherry to Character**
- Mood: Precise yet poetic; premium documentary craft meets sensory transformation.
- Layout: Museum-like process board across a 5-column grid: cherry, washed bean, drying bed, green bean, roasted bean; each stage presented as a cinematic specimen.
- Visual: High-resolution macro objects photographed on textured handmade paper; delicate arrows and minimal diagram lines connect each transformation stage.
- FX: Sequential reveal from left to right; arrows draw in like ink; beans softly rotate or shimmer with micro highlights; final roasted bean receives a subtle golden halo.
- Color: Cream paper base, botanical green, cherry crimson, parchment tan, espresso brown, restrained gold accents.
- Type: Sophisticated serif title top left; stage names in clean uppercase sans-serif; sensory notes in tiny italic annotations beneath each object.

**Slide 8 — The Ceremony of Smoke & Silence**
- Mood: Sacred, intimate, time-slowing; the Ethiopian coffee ceremony as a cinematic ritual of hospitality, memory, and community.
- Layout: Full-bleed documentary photograph on the left 70%; right 30% in warm parchment panel with sparse editorial notes. A thin vertical rule separates image and text like a luxury magazine feature.
- Visual: Low-angle scene of a woman roasting green coffee beans over charcoal; curling incense smoke, woven grass on the floor, jebena pot silhouetted in the background, small porcelain cups arranged like constellations.
- FX: Slow smoke drift animation; soft flicker of charcoal glow; text appears one line at a time like quiet narration; subtle film grain and lens-breathing zoom.
- Color: Charcoal black, roasted umber, incense gray, warm ivory, ember orange highlights.
- Type: Large elegant serif title top-right; small mono captions labeling “roast,” “grind,” “brew,” “serve”; poetic pull quote in italic serif near bottom: “Coffee is not consumed here — it is welcomed.”

**Slide 9 — Jebena: The Shape of Hospitality**
- Mood: Museum-like, premium, tactile; treating the traditional clay jebena as both design object and cultural vessel.
- Layout: Centered hero object composition on a deep matte background; exploded-view annotations orbit the jebena in fine editorial lines. Bottom strip shows three tiny cinematic frames: pouring, steam, first cup.
- Visual: Hyper-detailed photograph/3D editorial rendering of a black clay jebena with steam rising from the spout; hand-drawn callouts explain clay body, long neck, curved spout, heat source, serving motion.
- FX: Steam gently curls upward; annotation lines draw in with gold ink; jebena rotates 3 degrees with parallax depth; soft spotlight pulse from above.
- Color: Deep espresso black, clay brown, antique gold, cream typography, faint red-cherry accent dots.
- Type: Oversized serif title aligned left; precise mono labels for object details; short body copy in refined sans-serif, set like a luxury product editorial.

**Slide 10 — Three Cups, Three Invitations**
- Mood: Rhythmic, ceremonial, emotionally warm; each cup representing a deeper layer of connection.
- Layout: Triptych layout with three vertical panels: **Abol**, **Tona**, **Baraka**. Each panel has a cup close-up, a micro-story, and one sensory descriptor.
- Visual: Macro photography of tiny cups being filled from a jebena; hands passing cups across a low table; popcorn, incense, and sunlight cutting through smoke in the background.
- FX: Sequential pour animation across the three panels; golden liquid highlight ripples inside each cup; panel transitions behave like turning magazine pages.
- Color: Cream porcelain, dark coffee brown, golden steam, soft green grass floor accents, muted terracotta.
- Type: Panel titles in tall cinematic serif; sensory words in italic display type: “arrival,” “conversation,” “blessing”; captions in small uppercase mono with generous tracking.

**Slide 11 — Women Who Carry the Origin**
- Mood: Human, dignified, powerful; a cinematic portrait chapter honoring the women central to harvesting, processing, roasting, and serving Ethiopian coffee.
- Layout: Premium editorial portrait grid: one large hero portrait occupying the left half; four smaller portraits stacked on the right with elegant name/location captions. A translucent quote band crosses the lower third.
- Visual: Documentary portraits of Ethiopian women farmers and ceremony hosts: hands sorting red cherries, faces lit by morning highland light, woven baskets, coffee drying beds, quiet confidence.
- FX: Gentle Ken Burns motion on each portrait; quote band fades in like a documentary subtitle; soft golden particles drift subtly as dust in sunlight.
- Color: Highland green, coffee cherry red, sunlit ochre, warm cream, deep shadow brown.
- Type: Hero quote in refined serif: “Every bean passes through hands that know the land.” Names and regions in mono captions; minimal sans-serif body text for context, never crowded.

**Slide 12 — The Market Before Sunrise**
- Mood: Quiet anticipation, smoky dawn air, human rhythm before the city wakes; cinematic, intimate, observational.
- Layout: Full-bleed documentary photograph with a narrow editorial text column anchored on the far right; small caption strip along the bottom like a premium magazine feature.
- Visual: Early-morning Ethiopian coffee market scene: burlap sacks stacked in soft silhouettes, hands weighing green beans, steam from roadside buna, warm lantern light cutting through blue dawn haze.
- FX: Slow Ken Burns push toward the merchant’s hands; subtle film grain; floating dust particles in the light beam; text fades in gently after image settles.
- Color: Deep indigo dawn, roasted brown, burlap beige, muted gold lantern glow, soft charcoal shadows.
- Type: Large elegant serif title placed vertically along the right margin; small mono captions for location, time, and market notes; minimal body copy in refined editorial sans.

**Slide 13 — Traceability as a Love Letter**
- Mood: Premium, transparent, reverent; turning supply-chain information into something poetic and trustworthy.
- Layout: Split composition: left side a cinematic portrait of a farmer holding parchment coffee; right side an elegant traceability diagram flowing from farm to washing station to exporter to roaster to cup.
- Visual: Hand-drawn route line over a textured map fragment of Ethiopia, layered with small documentary photo cards, origin tags, altitude markers, varietal notes, and processing icons.
- FX: Route line animates like ink being drawn across paper; origin cards softly rise into place; tiny glowing points pulse at each stage of the journey.
- Color: Warm parchment, coffee brown, highland green, soft ivory, restrained gold accents, subtle red coffee-cherry highlights.
- Type: Serif headline large and calm at top right; mono micro-labels for data points; italic pull quote near the portrait: “A name, a place, a harvest, a hand.”

**Slide 14 — The Future Grows in the Highlands**
- Mood: Hopeful, cinematic, forward-looking; resilience, climate awareness, young farmers, innovation rooted in tradition.
- Layout: Magazine-style triptych: three tall vertical panels showing land, people, and innovation; bottom band reserved for three concise insight cards.
- Visual: Panel 1: misty terraced coffee hills; Panel 2: young Ethiopian agronomist inspecting leaves; Panel 3: solar drying beds or quality lab cupping table. Add subtle overlay of contour lines and climate data traces.
- FX: Panels reveal one by one with soft shutter-like wipes; faint animated contour lines drift slowly; insight cards glow subtly on hover/entrance.
- Color: Highland green, mist gray, warm cream, clay red, muted sky blue, golden sunlight accents.
- Type: Bold editorial serif headline across the top spanning all three panels; insight cards in clean sans; key words highlighted in cherry red and gold.

**Slide 15 — Every Cup Returns to Origin**
- Mood: Emotional finale, sacred stillness, cinematic closure; the feeling of holding an entire landscape in one cup.
- Layout: Full-bleed closing hero image with centered title; small closing line at bottom center; generous negative space created by steam and shadow.
- Visual: Close-up of Ethiopian coffee poured from a jebena into small cups, steam rising like mist over distant highlands subtly double-exposed inside the steam.
- FX: Slow-motion steam animation; gentle golden light bloom; title fades in letter by letter; final transition holds in silence with soft film grain.
- Color: Espresso black, clay terracotta, golden amber, warm ivory, faint mist blue, deep roasted brown.
- Type: Large cinematic serif centered: “Every Cup Returns to Origin”; delicate italic subtitle beneath; tiny mono footer: “Ethiopia — birthplace, ritual, future.”
